annotations.text:
SHELL 1 — COACH
A dashboard is the front door. Four tabs: Home, Workouts, Progress, Profile.

For: the app has something to say on rest days, so it earns a reason to open. Density justifies a tab bar, and the bar makes the other screens discoverable without a tour.

Against: it promises four destinations V1 does not have yet. Starting a workout is a button among many, not the point of the screen.

Resume: banner on Home, you choose.

SHELL 2 — DOCK
No tab bar. One scroll of cards, and a dock pinned above the home indicator that is always the next action.

For: one persistent affordance instead of stub destinations. The dock changes state rather than the screen changing — idle it starts a workout, live it is the session controller, visible from anywhere.

Against: everything except Start is a card you must scroll to. Adding a fifth destination later means redesigning the stack.

Resume: the dock becomes the session bar.

SHELL 3 — LEDGER
The record is the app. Home is the training log, reverse-chronological, with today as the first actionable row.

For: a tracker's value is what it has already recorded. Every row carries real numbers, so the screen is useful rather than decorative, and 'what did I lift last Thursday' is answered without navigating.

Against: least motivational of the three, and it leans on a FAB for the primary action, which is the weakest place to put a verb.

Resume: today's row goes live in place.

These screens are drawn against Shell 1's chrome, since it is the only option with a tab bar to draw. Library and History show the bar because they are destinations; Session, Exercise detail and Summary are pushed, so they have none. Under Shell 2 or 3 the same screens keep their content and lose or swap the bar — the choice of shell does not change these layouts.

Active session is the screen that matters most: the set table shows previous values inline, and the two steppers put weight and reps under a thumb without a keyboard. Both the rest banner and the active-session state are toggles on the artboard.

The vocabulary every artboard is built from, plus the states the UI-hygiene checklist in CLAUDE.md requires — skeletons that match their row, empty states that offer a way out, error states with retry, toasts, and a confirm dialog with a verb-specific label instead of OK.

The accent is a single token. Flip it on any artboard to compare the lime direction against the web app's existing Spotify green.
